about.title: El Segundo Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: El Segundo is a small city, but its stretch of roadway sees a steady flow of traffic feeding into Los Angeles County — Pacific Coast Highway, Sepulveda Boulevard, Imperial Highway, and Douglas Street among them. Public records show 85 injury collisions and 106 injured people in the most recent final crash year, with Wednesday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. showing up often. Behind every one of those numbers is someone dealing with medical bills, missed work, and an insurance adjuster who may call before the person has even seen a doctor. We're here to help. Our team handles personal injury claims and works on a contingency basis, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery.
about.ctaText: Tell us what happened — a free case review is confidential and at no cost.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Soon After an El Segundo Crash

items.title: California's Clock Is Already Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury lawsuit in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government vehicle or roadway defect was involved. We can help sort out which deadline applies to your situation early.

items.title: Comparative Fault Rules Reward Careful Documentation
items.desc: California lets you recover damages even if you're partly at fault, with your compensation reduced by your share of responsibility. Because fault percentages are often disputed, we document evidence and push back on lowball assumptions to help protect your claim.

items.title: No Cap Means the Details of Your Case Matter More
items.desc: California places no limit on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in most car accident cases, so how your claim is presented and supported can carry real weight. We can help make sure your account of pain, disruption, and recovery isn't undersold to an insurer.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company already called asking for a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: It's generally wise to avoid giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer before speaking with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to minimize your claim later. We can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: Is Pacific Coast Highway or Sepulveda Boulevard more likely to be involved in a crash near El Segundo?
items.answer: Public collision records for El Segundo list Pacific Coast Highway, Sepulveda Boulevard, Imperial Highway, and Douglas Street among the higher-volume corridors for reported crashes. That doesn't mean any one road is more or less risky, just that these are frequently traveled routes. What matters most for your claim is the specific facts of your accident.

items.question: What does it cost to get a free case review?
items.answer: Nothing. Our case review is free, and we work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront fee to have your case reviewed.
